body_markdown:
It’s not often that a manufacturer refreshes both its light-duty and heavy-duty pickup lines in the same year. That’s why we were surprised that Chevrolet, fresh on the heels of an all-new[Silverado 1500](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2027-chevrolet-silverado-1500-marks-the-return-of-the-350-and-400-v-8s/) , was also debuting its new turbodiesel V-8 in the 2027 Silverado 2500 and 3500. Chevy brought us out to Tucson, Arizona, to drive the new 2027 Silverado HD and test it out off-road, on the highway, and towing more than 30,000 pounds.


DW Burnett


Chevrolet


While the[2027 Silverado 1500](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2027-chevrolet-silverado-1500-marks-the-return-of-the-350-and-400-v-8s/) gets new sheet metal outside and a new dash and interior inside, the HD models will carry on looking like their 2026 predecessors. All of the updates happen under the skin. The biggest news for the 2027 Silverado HD, literally, was the addition of the 8.3-liter L6P Duramax V-8 that replaces the 6.6-liter L5P Duramax across the Silverado HD lineup. Before we even drove the new diesel, we spoke with Rob Moran, assistant chief engineer for the 8.3L Duramax. He’s been working on the big V-8 for the past three and a half years, but it’s been in development for even longer. He gave us a look at some of the engine’s burly internal parts as well as its exhaust system.


The L6P’s 555-horsepower output is an 85-hp increase, leapfrogging the 500-hp 6.7L Powerstroke V-8 offered in the Ford Super Duty and leaving the 430-hp 6.7L Cummins inline-six Ram way behind. With a price of $11,400, it’s also more affordable than the diesel options from Ford and Ram


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


While there are plenty of design similarities, like its pushrod, 16-valve cylinder heads and crank-driven water pump, this[“Mongoose” diesel](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/make-way-for-mongoose-gms-new-duramax-turbodiesel-displaces-a-whopping-8-3-liters/) isn’t just a bored and stroked version of any previous engine. This is an all-new powerplant built on lessons learned from the past 25-plus years of the Duramax V-8. The foundation of the 8.3L Duramax is its compacted graphite iron (CGI) block, which is cast in Germany. “The block for an 8.3 weighs basically the same as the current 6.6-liter L5P block,” said Moran. That’s a big win considering the 8.3L is larger in virtually every dimension than the 6.6L it replaces, with an increase in bore spacing and deck height.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


The L6P now uses an air-to-water charge cooler, replacing the previous air-to-air charge cooling system.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


With 555 horsepower, the Mongoose makes the 2027 Silverado HD the current leader in the 3/4- and 1-ton diesel pickup horsepower war, yet its specific output—the engine’s power output per liter—is down compared to that of the L5P Duramax it’s replacing. Moran said a culmination of things led to the new, bigger, but lower-stressed V-8 diesel. “From an emissions perspective, when you look at the current engine, the L5P, we were really at a point where specific power was about as high as we could get it for the NOx, for the emissions number we were trying to hit. We really couldn’t make more power without going to a larger engine.” He said that going to a larger engine that was stressed a bit less allowed for the engine tuning to be more efficient, so we can expect the Mongoose to return slightly better fuel economy, especially when towing. “We were able to get to a point where we have more headroom to allow the calibrators to manipulate what we’re doing with air and fuel and EGR in order to get the cleanest, most efficient combustion we can.”


The 8.3-liter’s forged steel crankshaft uses massive rod journals that feature rolled fillets and laser-hardened surfaces to stand up to the forces exerted on each power stroke. “If you look at any heavy-duty diesel engine, they nearly all have angle-split rods,” said Moran. “We’ve been doing that for years, since the ’17 L5P.” The angle split may look strange if you’re used to seeing gasoline connecting rods. Without this angle split, the rods wouldn’t fit down the bore.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


## Specs: 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 2500 ZR2


**Pricing:** $77,695/$89,095 (base ZR2/as-tested)
**Powertrain** : 8.3-liter turbodiesel pushrod V-8, ten-speed automatic transmission
**Output:** 555 hp @ 2500 rpm; 1230 lb-ft @ 1400 rpm
**Layout:** Four-wheel-drive, four-door, five-passenger pickup truck
**Weight:** 8400 lb (est.)
**EPA-rated Fuel Economy:** TBA
**Competition:**[Ford Super Duty](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ford-expands-super-dutys-off-road-and-luxury-options-for-2027/) ,[Ram Heavy Duty](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ram-stuffs-1075-lb-ft-cummins-diesel-into-2027-power-wagon/)


DW Burnett


“One of the key things with this new system,” Moran said, as he showed us the Duramax’s new exhaust, “we’ve increased the volume significantly. Larger catalyst volume means the gas spends more time in there to react, which makes them more efficient. That efficiency has allowed us to have more latitude with the way the engine’s performing.” Not only does the larger Duramax engine run cleaner, it also runs cooler, too. “At rated power on the new engine, we’re 30 or 40 degrees cooler in exhaust temperature than we were previously.”


Besides the power to get loads moving, trucks need serious brakes to get a monster tow rating. Chevy ditched sliding calipers for four-piston fixed calipers and 14.6-inch front rotors.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


Although the Silverado 1500 gets[all-new, Gen VI gasoline engines](https://www.hagerty.com/media/new-car-reviews/2027-chevrolet-silverado-1500-marks-the-return-of-the-350-and-400-v-8s/) with an increased compression ratio to go with their new cylinder heads and taller deck height, and the optional Mongoose Duramax is big news under the hood of the Silverado HD, that truck’s base engine remains the Gen V 6.6-liter V-8. It does bring more power and torque, however, thanks to a new intake manifold. Dubbed “Turbo-Jet” as an homage to big-blocks of the past, the new intake helps increase output from last year’s 401 hp and 464 lb-ft of torque to 412 hp and 472 lb-ft of torque. That name’s not the engine’s only link to big-blocks of the past; it’s built at the same Tonawanda, New York, assembly plant as 427s and 454s from the 1960s and ’70s.


## Behind the Wheel


Besides the improved gas V-8 and all-new Duramax, the biggest changes in the 2027 Silverado HD are the switch to electric power steering and electrically boosted power brakes—both firsts in the heavy-duty pickup market. The steering improvement can be felt immediately, with better feedback on-road that can also be dampened when towing or when running at low-speed off-road. The braking feel is also upgraded, with a firm pedal that requires less travel overall. That reduced travel allows the brake pedal to be nearly on the same plane as the throttle. It’s a small change but one that can reduce driver fatigue on long trips.


DW Burnett


DW Burnett


Although we did drive a new High Country Duramax at altitude, we spent most of our time in the HD behind the wheel of a new ZR2. With its factory suspension lift and 35-inch off-road tires, it’s a climb getting into the cab, even for occupants over six feet tall. Our Duramax-powered ZR2 surprised us with its quiet idle and linear power curve. It built boost quickly to get up to highway speed, and even with the 35s, it seemed quieter than some of its competitors’ off-road offerings. When unladen, the 10-speed automatic keeps the engine speeds low and calm. It’s not as smooth as its light-duty counterpart, and it also lacks a front differential locker. Still, its DSSV dampers deliver a great ride on rough trails and on the pavement. The ride quality is in another league compared to its solid-axle HD brethren from Ford and Dodge.


DW Burnett


Chevy gave us a chance to try a Silverado 3500 loaded up close to its maximum tow rating of 38,000 pounds. To give anyone a shot at that kind of pulling power, including those who might not be used to such a heavy load, Chevy put the truck on a dragstrip. Even with 555 hp on tap, the sticky track surface wasn’t necessary. We watched several members of the media hop in and floor the accelerator as the Silverado and its trailer rumbled up to speed. Time and time again, the Duramax and 10-speed combo managed to get the massive trailer to about 60 mph before it took the first turnout and headed back. When it was our turn, we rolled into the throttle and then floored it, letting the 10-speed keep the big diesel spooled up. As impressive as the acceleration was, the new brakes also deserve praise, as they felt linear and easily up to the task of keeping the trailer under control. For big downhill braking, the Duramax also has an exhaust brake to take some of the strain off and keep things cool.


This latest, turbocharged salvo has put the Bow Tie brand at the top of the diesel hierarchy. Ram, the brand that kicked off the diesel performance wars with a 5.9-liter Cummins, is now using a four-valve, 6.7-liter evolution of the Cummins. Ford’s V-8 Powerstroke also displaces 6.7 liters. They’re both likely running into the same limitations that led GM to develop a larger engine. Ford is rumored to be working on a V-8 turbodiesel in the 8.0-liter range, and Ram can’t rest on its laurels. We’re always due for another round of one-upmanship, but for now the Mongoose reigns.


## 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 2500 ZR2


**Highs:** 8.3L Mongoose Duramax has tremendous pulling power; the proven 6.6L gas engine returns; steering and braking feel great.


**Lows:** We’ll have to wait for a new look and the interior upgrades from the Silverado 1500.


**Takeaway:** The Mongoose Duramax has big shoes to fill, but its smooth, responsive 555 hp makes the Silverado HD the new king of diesel power.
